_comment_purpose: TEMPLATE — CONTAINS NO REAL VALUES. This describes the TorBox resolver side of a real-provider run. It is documentation of what to place, not a file to copy into service unchanged: every REPLACE-ME must be replaced, and the preflight refuses the file while any remain.
_comment_where: Place the real files under a 0700 directory. The default the gate looks in, and the only place it EVER looks, is /mnt/user/appdata/catalog/secrets/real-provider/. The gate never searches the filesystem for anything that might be a credential, never reads one from the environment, and never prompts.
_comment_files: FOUR FILES, ALL MODE 0600. Note that TWO of them hold secrets and they are different values: `torbox-credential` is your API key and only the resolver reads it; `credential` is the gate secret the daemon presents to the resolver.

files.torbox-credential: The TorBox API key and nothing else. NOTE WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A USUAL TOKEN: TorBox authenticates requestdl with a ?token= QUERY PARAMETER, so the request URL is itself a bearer credential. Anything that logs a request URL publishes this key. The resolver never logs, stores or returns a request URL, and refuses any credential file whose mode has group or other bits set.
files.credential: THE GATE SECRET, and note the name: this is the file `deploy/projection-real-provider-gate.sh` reads, and for a TorBox run it must hold the GATE SECRET rather than your TorBox key. The gate talks to the loopback resolver, not to TorBox; only the resolver ever sees your API key. Generate it locally, e.g. `head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'`. It is NOT your TorBox key and must not be.
files.gate-secret-note: Any high-entropy string you generate locally, e.g. `head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'`. The projection daemon presents this to the resolver as a bearer. It is NOT your TorBox key and must not be. Two secrets exist so the data-plane binary — the one that talks to arbitrary provider-supplied CDN hosts — never holds the credential that can manage your whole TorBox account.
files.objects.json: 1-3 objects you are legally entitled to. See deploy/real-provider-objects.template.json. Each `ref` is a TorBox stable reference, described below. TREAT THIS FILE AS A SECRET: a reference identifies an item in your account.
files.endpoint.json: See deploy/real-provider-endpoint.template.json, filled in as shown under `endpointShape` below.

_comment_ref: THE STABLE REFERENCE FORMAT. `torbox:<kind>:<providerId>:<fileId>` — the minimum TorBox's own endpoints need, and deliberately nothing else. No name, hash, size or category: each would be one more field to keep out of logs forever, and none is needed to fetch bytes.
_comment_ids: Both ids are plain non-negative integers. The item id is the torrent/web/usenet id TorBox shows for the item; the file id is the index of the file within it. Get both from your own TorBox dashboard or from a read-only listing you already have — this gate never lists your account.
_comment_endpoint: HOW endpoint.json MUST LOOK FOR A TORBOX RUN. resolverUrl points at the LOOPBACK resolver this repository runs, not at TorBox: the daemon talks to the resolver, the resolver talks to TorBox. allowedOrigins names the CDN origins TorBox may hand back — the daemon refuses to dial anything else, and re-checks every address at dial time.
_comment_origins_resolver: THE RESOLVER ORIGIN MUST BE IN THIS LIST TOO, and it is easy to miss. The daemon checks EVERY url it is about to dial against the allowlist, and the resolver is one of them -- omit it and the daemon refuses to start with "origin not in endpoint allowlist", naming the resolver rather than any CDN host.
_comment_origins_hard: FINDING THE RIGHT CDN allowedOrigins IS THE ONE STEP THAT NEEDS CARE. TorBox mints CDN links on hosts that can differ by account and region, and the daemon will refuse a link whose origin is not listed — which is the behaviour you want, but it means a first run can fail closed on a host you did not anticipate. Resolve one object by hand first and list exactly the origin it returns. Do NOT widen this to a bare wildcard; an unbounded allowlist is how a signed URL becomes an SSRF.
_comment_run: COMMANDS. Nothing below takes a secret as an argument; every one takes a PATH.

commands.3-preflight-gate: npm run go:real-provider-gate  (skips with 77 until all inputs are present)

_comment_never: WHAT THIS ADAPTER WILL NEVER DO, whatever it is asked: create, control, edit, delete or download a provider job; request a permalink; list or export your account; or set redirect=true. The only verb is GET, on the three requestdl paths, and the only effect is that TorBox opens an existing file's link for a while.
